title: Delivery Claims Evidence Rules: Deadline, Signed Declaration and Police Report
content:
Desk guidance on the evidence a Delivery Claims claim must carry before it goes to decision.

## The rule

1. Every type of evidence the claim type requires must be logged on the claim before it goes to decision.
2. The evidence must be on the claim no later than the claim type's evidence deadline in calendar days after the claim was opened; otherwise the claim is denied with the reason evidence missing.
3. On a Delivered Not Received Claim whose claimed value is at or above the claim type's declaration threshold, the customer's signed non-receipt declaration is also required. The customer signs it personally; the agent cannot sign it or attest it on the customer's behalf.
4. At or above the claim type's police report threshold, a police report reference is required as well.
5. A Damaged in Transit claimant keeps the item and its packaging for the claim type's retention period in days.
6. Evidence references are recorded exactly as given — the upload, declaration, report or trace reference as the customer or carrier supplied it.
7. Evidence is logged only while the claim is in status opened, carrier trace, under review or denied.

## Kinds of evidence a claim can carry

Damage photos, packaging photos, a wrong item photo, a neighbour check confirmation, the customer's signed declaration, a police report reference and a carrier trace result. For a line-scope claim, each piece of evidence is recorded against the order line it concerns.

## Claim status and evidence

| Claim status | Evidence may be logged |
|---|---|
| opened | yes |
| carrier trace | yes |
| under review | yes |
| denied | yes |
| approved | no |
| resolved | no |
| withdrawn | no |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- With a deadline of 7 calendar days, a claim opened on 4 April has its evidence in time if it is on the claim by 11 April; evidence first logged on 12 April is late and the claim is denied for evidence missing.
- A Delivered Not Received Claim with a claimed value exactly at the declaration threshold needs the signed declaration; one cent below it does not. The same holds at the police report threshold.
- A declaration the agent completed for the customer does not satisfy the rule: only the customer's own signature does.
